text:
Predicates:
SuperheroMovie(x) ::: x is a superhero movie.
GoodGuy(x) ::: x is a good guy.
BadGuy(x) ::: x is a bad guy.
Fight(x, y) ::: x fights y.
Nemesis(x, y) ::: x is the nemesis of y.
Win(x) ::: x wins.
NamedAfter(x, y) ::: x is named after y.
Premises:
∀x (SuperheroMovie(x) → ∃y (GoodGuy(y) ∧ Win(y))) ::: In superhero movies, the good guys always win.
SuperheroMovie(theSurprisingAdventuresOfSirDigbyChickenCaesar) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is a superhero movie.
∀x ∀y (GoodGuy(x) ∧ BadGuy(y) → Fight(x, y)) ∧ ∀x ∀y (BadGuy(x) ∧ GoodGuy(y) → Fight(x, y)) ::: Good guys fight bad guys and vice versa.
Fight(sirDigby, sirDigbysNemesis) ∧ Nemesis(sirDigbysNemesis, sirDigby) ::: Sir Digby fights his nemesis.
∀x ∀y (SuperheroMovie(x) ∧ NamedAfter(x, y) → GoodGuy(y)) ::: If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character is a good guy.
NamedAfter(theSurprisingAdventuresOfSirDigbyChickenCaesar, sirDigby) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is named after Sir Digby.
∀x ∀y (Win(x) ∧ Fight(x, y) → ¬Win(y)) ::: If somebody wins a fight, the person they are fighting does not win.
∀x ∀y (SuperheroMovie(x) ∧ NamedAfter(x, y) → ∃z (x = z)) ::: If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character is in the movie.
Conclusion:
¬Win(sirDigbysNemesis) ::: Sir Digby's nemesis does not win.
